To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

children who are in the lower reading group choose more children from the higher reading group, and children who are in a higher reading group choose more of their own peers and fewer children from the lower group.

the lower group members chose fewer children from their own group and more children from the top group, the middle group members chose more top group members than expected and fewer bottom group members than expected, the top group members chose more bottom group members than top group members and fewer middle group members than expected.
the reading groups are psychologically important to children in first grade, and the reading groups are the only enduring group in the classroom.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social psychological processes that underlie group membership.
the social psychology of reading groups.
a particular type of psychological group, a reading group, and its relation to the social group structure of the elementary classroom.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

reading groups are psychological groups, that is to say, that the reading groups are the only enduring groups in the classes, and that they have a definite psychological impact on the children in the classes.
the children's choices were not determined by their reading groups.
the reading groups were psychologically real groups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reading groups in the first grade were the only stable social groups in the classes.

the children in the top reading group were the most popular, and that the children in lower groups tended to choose children who were in the same group, and to avoid children in the other reading groups.
the reading groups are psychologically important groups for children in the elementary grades.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reading groups were the primary groups of the classes, and they were the primary basis of the children’s social choices. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2017 APA, all rights reserved)
